purpose: Single source-index of 215 new religious art object/inventory leads through wave 14. Covers painted studies/linked wings as explicit art objects; 8 old acquired official masters; 0 production approvals.

policy.rating: 0–2 artworks excluded, 3 can be revisited, existing acquired 4–5 never re-source, 5 needed repeated use; past unnumbered subject selection ≠ 5.
policy.objectIdentity: Museum/owner plus accession+title, never subject name alone; source URL shared by distinct works is fine, but repeated URL within one institutional listing does NOT count proof of a unique object without name accession corroboration.
policy.provenance: Only verified original autograph oil painting rows are candidates for acquisition; works 'after', studio and prints held separately.
policy.artistCorpusCompletion: No claim of full Rubens / Van Dyck global oeuvre; Louvre Van Dyck holdings specifically audited; Prado Apostle series complete.
policy.rights: Digital reproduction worldwide commercial rights, pixel dimensions, fidelity and crop must be checked after artwork identity. Public-domain object alone does not clear copyrighted image.
policy.attribution: Physical identity and attribution independent; W10-003, W10-009, W10-011 held before original-autograph eligibility.
policy.collectionCoverage: Still incomplete for Nancy full holdings and worldwide oeuvres; no user artistic approvals implied.
policy.oneObjectManyScenes: One work may depict several episodes and later non-historical devotional figures; preserve separate scene associations without duplicating painting original or asserting biblical historicity.
policy.champaigne: Separate Philippe vs Jean-Baptiste de Champaigne: W12-005 has Louvre-recorded dominant Jean-Baptiste execution, W12-006 origin to verify, W12-008 proposed authorship only. Saint-Flour and Libourne Pentecost are NOT identical objects.
policy.majorAttributionConflict: Coup de Lance London L1121 still Rubens in NG catalogue vs Van Dyck in KMSKA technical research; record dissent and verify before original-artist repeat. KMSKA 297 authentically recorded under Van Dyck. NGA Boeckhorst 52251 exclude from Van Dyck autograph originals. Corrected NGA Jan Boeckhorst accession 1970.17.107, object page ID 52251, not inventory '52251'.
policy.physicalWorkAndEnsemble: Vienna GG678 and GG698 share an Ildefonso altarpiece ensemble yet have distinct museum inventories; separate individual artwork components and scene crossrefs, no double counting entire commission. Sketches and final canvases separate physical objects.
policy.disputedCaravaggio: Genoa PB1638 Ecce Homo must remain disputed attribution, although museum currently Caravaggio; unrelated Madrid Prado loan object W07-015 and Cigoli painting. Montserrat Saint Jerome official museum acceptance.
policy.originalityScope: Research unique physical inventory leads include genuine Rubens studies and works of workshop execution; do not collapse scope to all-autograph oils count.
policy.artistAttributionCaution: KHM Ignatius GG517 is Rubens plus workshop attribution (possible Jordaens); Xavier GG519 workshop execution is under review, not conclusively segmented.

queue.title: Le Christ mort sur la Croix
queue.provenanceNotes: 1655 oil commissioned for Grande Chartreuse; Christ shown dead. Distinct from Louvre earlier living Christ on Cross INV 1126 and smaller INV1127 workshop replica.

queue.title: La Pentecôte ou La Descente du Saint-Esprit (Saint-Flour)
queue.provenanceNotes: Palissy Monument historique proposes, DOES NOT fully certify, Champaigne original. Possible 1628 Carmelite cycle panel. Different from Libourne B720 falsely attributed to Champaigne in past, now Verdier/Plattemontagne. Attribution hold.

queue.title: Les Pèlerins d'Emmaüs (Nantes)
queue.provenanceNotes: Distinct Nantes original catalogued as Philippe de Champaigne in Louvre deposit; compare with different original same subject by Eustache Le Sueur at Grenoble before asserting visual identity.

queue.title: La Samaritaine / Christ et la Samaritaine
queue.provenanceNotes: Circa 1650 original Caen oil on canvas 114.5×113cm, Port-Royal high altar ensemble of three. Do not confuse with 17th-century copies in other churches or anonymous French paintings.

queue.title: Saint Martin Dividing his Cloak (Zaventem original)
queue.provenanceNotes: Municipality confirms local altar painting c.1621 by Van Dyck. Not Royal Collection RCIN405878 and NOT NGA Jan Boeckhorst attributed sketch.

queue.title: Saint Martin Dividing his Cloak (Windsor original)
queue.provenanceNotes: Distinct larger oil on canvas around 1620, preserved at Windsor; royal collection identity corroborated by National Gallery technical bulletin and Royal Collection catalogue references. Royal Collection web detail inaccessible in this research environment; image permissions required.

queue.title: Christ on the Cross with Saint Catherine of Siena, Saint Dominic and an Angel
queue.institution: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1622–1627 original oil on canvas, 313.8×244.6cm. Mystical saint presence is devotional, not the historical crucifixion eyewitness list.

queue.title: Saint Augustine in Ecstasy (large altarpiece)
queue.institution: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1628 oil on canvas 383.5×220.6 cm, original side altar commission for Augustinian Antwerp church. Separate physical object from oil study inv5145.

queue.title: Saint Augustine in Ecstasy (preparatory oil study)
queue.institution: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1628 original oil-on-panel study 44.5×27.5cm; separate from full-size altarpiece IB003. Preserve 'study' role and do not count as separate devotional iconographic episode.

queue.title: Christ on the Cross, Le Coup de Lance (KMSKA altarpiece)
queue.institution: Royal Museum of Fine Arts Antwerp (KMSKA)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1620 oil on panel altarpiece 429.6×310cm, formerly Rubens, **currently KMSKA assigned Van Dyck**. The 2011 technical assessment identified Van Dyck design/execution for Rubens' workshop. Distinct from V&A/NG London L1121 oil-on-oak modello.

queue.title: St Ambrose and Emperor Theodosius
queue.provenanceNotes: Religious-historical painting c.1615/16, physically distinct from Van Dyck National Gallery London NG50 St Ambrose and Theodosius.

queue.title: Penitent Saint Magdalene and Her Sister Martha
queue.provenanceNotes: KHM correctly notes historical conflation of Mary of Bethany, Mary Magdalene and repentant sinful woman in Counter-Reformation iconography; do not claim same biblical identity as an exegetical fact.

queue.title: The Infant Christ with Saint John the Baptist and Two Angels
queue.provenanceNotes: KHM identifies the childhood devotional ensemble, circa 1615/20; NOT an incident explicitly narrated in canonical Gospels. Berlin Gemäldegalerie inventory 779 is RUBENS WORKSHOP REPLICA, not same original. Some still-life details may be collaboration.

queue.title: The Miracles of Saint Ignatius of Loyola (oil modello)
queue.provenanceNotes: KHM 2025 scholar identifies genuine Rubens preparatory modello distinct from finished GG 517 massive altarpiece; 1615–1617 approximate. No conflation of sketch and altarpiece.

queue.title: The Miracles of Saint Ignatius of Loyola (large altarpiece)
queue.provenanceNotes: KHM scholarly publication attributes monumental altarpiece to Rubens AND workshop, proposes Jacob Jordaens participation as stylistic inference NOT documented fact. Distinct from Rubens modello GG530; never sole Rubens autograph.

queue.title: The Miracles of Saint Francis Xavier (oil modello)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1616/17 official KHM supplied Google Arts and Culture object, original study, distinct from huge altarpiece GG519 and from Saint Ignatius study GG530.

queue.artist: Peter Paul Rubens (workshop execution under review)
queue.title: The Miracles of Saint Francis Xavier (large altarpiece)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1617/18 very large Jesuit high-altar picture. KHM scholarly essay notes two groups likely worked on paired altarpieces (GG517/GG519); do not certify fully autograph, workshop involvement attribution scope under review.

queue.title: The Assumption of the Virgin (Vienna early altarpiece)
queue.provenanceNotes: c.1614–1621 Vienna oil original was intended for Antwerp Cathedral, hung in Jesuit church 1621–1776. DIFFERENT physical artwork from later Antwerp Cathedral Assumption W06-004 and NGA assumption entry artist compound.

queue.title: Lamentation of Christ by the Virgin and Saint John (large panel)
queue.provenanceNotes: c.1614/15, oak 107.5×115.5cm. Distinct FROM KHM small Lamentation GG515, and distinct from Rubens Antwerp Descent from Cross; iconography blends Passion events.

queue.title: The Lamentation (small oil-on-oak panel)
queue.provenanceNotes: c.1614 oil on oak 40.5×52.5cm; KHM press catalogue identity; DIFFERENT object from larger lamentation GG529. Label 'small original oil panel' not duplicate full painting.

queue.title: Triptych of Saint Ildefonso (central scene and donor wings)
queue.provenanceNotes: c.1630–32 triptych: Virgin presents chasuble to St Ildefonso (not crown). Donors Albert and Isabella on wings with saint patrons. Components mapped as different iconographic scenes of one triptych.

queue.title: The Holy Family Beneath an Apple Tree (outer Ildefonso wings)
queue.provenanceNotes: Separate museum inventory GG698 = two joined exterior wing images originally belonging to Ildefonso altar GG678. PART OF SAME COMMISSION/ENSEMBLE, not a second independent Rubens altarpiece. Count separate physical artwork inventory/photography target but same ensemble ID.

queue.title: The Capture of Samson (Vienna original)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1628–30, distinct from Rubens NG London Samson & Delilah W03-003. KHM names Anthony van Dyck; historical inventory GG512.

queue.title: Vision of the Blessed Hermann Joseph with the Virgin
queue.provenanceNotes: 1629/30 commissioned by Jesuit bachelors' confraternity, separate from Rosalia Peter Paul KHM GG482. A medieval Premonstratensian legend, NOT biblical event.

queue.title: Madonna and Child with Saints Rosalia, Peter and Paul
queue.provenanceNotes: 1629 original KHM GG482 described in its institution-authored contextual note on companion GG488. NOT same composition as Metropolitan Saint Rosalia W03-005, nor NGA Virgin as Intercessor.

queue.title: Apostle Judas Thaddeus (Böhler series)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1619–1621 original Van Dyck panel 61.4×49.7cm, distinct KHM GG9702 Simon. 13 painting Böhler apostolic series NOT completed by this two-item KHM census.

queue.title: Apostle Simon (Böhler series)
queue.provenanceNotes: 1619–1621 original panel, 64×51.5cm, one of 13 Van Dyck Christ-and-Apostles Böhler series; separate portrait from Simon in Rubens Prado apostle series W05-010.

queue.title: Saint Jerome Penitent (Montserrat original)
queue.provenanceNotes: Official Museum of Montserrat identifies Caravaggio original dated 1605, oil 145.5×101.5cm; distinct from Borghese GG056, Valletta Saint Jerome and other versions. Do not treat all St Jerome works as one.

queue.title: Ecce Homo (Palazzo Bianco, Genoa)
queue.institution: Musei di Strada Nuova, Palazzo Bianco, Genoa
queue.provenanceNotes: Genoa official catalogue lists Caravaggio while museum narrative admits serious attribution disputes; wartime paint damage and subsequent integrative restoration. Distinct from Prado loan Ecce Homo W07-015 and from other copies. Must NOT count confirmed autograph, acquisition gate contested.
